properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev/docs toolchain only — the ordinals API's runtime server tree never reaches hash.js; it ships with redoc-cli, used by the `generate:docs` script.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Feeds components/postgres/src/lib.rs connections; whether MD5 auth is actually negotiated depends on the Postgres server's pg_hba.conf — postgres-protocol supports both. Changeable here by requiring SCRAM on the server.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev/docs toolchain only (redoc-cli, semantic-release trees); the runtime API servers never import this stack, but the legacy KDF is what that stack would use to derive AES keys if invoked.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev tooling (sshpk chain); kept as a shipped dev-tree KDF capability. The collector's 'bcrypt password hashing' label is refined here: this is bcrypt_pbkdf, not bcrypt-the-password-hash.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Public-data equality on locally stored blockchain identifiers; would only matter if a secret-dependent comparison were ever added at these sites. Not a MAC verification against attacker-controlled input.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is Bitcoin's consensus curve: quantum-vulnerable (Shor) but replaceable only by a Bitcoin protocol change, not by this repo — observable, not changeable here. Signature verification itself happens inside the external bitcoind node. The linked secp256k1 crate (Cargo.lock:3440) is reported as a separate finding.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-fixture generator: Math.random produces fake txid/block-hash strings for test DB rows; no keys, tokens, nonces or verifiers derive from it. Contrast: the Rust side's only rand use (components/ordinals/src/db/blocks.rs:141, rand 0.9 ThreadRng = ChaCha12, OS-seeded) is retry-backoff jitter — no weak-PRNG issue there. Cosmetic fix if ever needed: crypto.getRandomValues; today it is C-rated test-only noise, kept so the inventory shows the fact with its true scope.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev-tree-only capability: redoc-cli bundles crypto-browserify, whose create-ecdh polyfill provides browser ECDH (via elliptic/bn.js). Neither API server imports crypto modules (verified: no createECDH/crypto require in api/*/src), and the runtime dependency set (fastify, postgres, bignumber, bitcoinjs-lib) does not reach create-ecdh. Classical ECDH ships in the npm dev install only — the B- retroactive-break rating describes the package, not a live session here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Capability-level row: on the Rust side ring serves rustls for TLS only (first-party code never calls ring:: directly); in the client lockfile tweetnacl sits in a dev-only chain and is not imported by the generated client code (its runtime deps are isomorphic-fetch only). Ed25519 → ML-DSA-65 applies to the shipped capability, not to any live signing call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is the classical key-agreement half of the indexer's TLS posture: the one live TLS client is components/bitcoind's build_http_client (reqwest 0.12 + rustls-tls) — it posts JSON-RPC to bitcoin_config.rpc_url with basic auth, and its only certificate posture control is danger_accept_invalid_certs(true) (reported separately as a new finding). Harvest-now-decrypt-later applies to any https deployment of that session; the default rpc_url is http://localhost:8332. The client-lock tweetnacl is dev

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev-only: elliptic is pulled by redoc-cli's crypto-browserify chain ("dev": true at every occurrence) for the docs bundler. The API's runtime dependency bitcoinjs-lib@6.1.0 does NOT depend on elliptic (v6 dropped it), so there is no runtime reach, and no first-party import of elliptic exists. ECDSA here is a shipped dev-tree capability, not an invoked one.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Browser PBKDF2 polyfill for the docs-generator toolchain; neither API source imports pbkdf2 or derives keys from passwords (grep over api/*/src finds no crypto module use at all). No first-party password KDF exists in this repo, so these entries carry no iteration-count or hash-choice decisions — a presence-only row.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Session-scoped auth MAC; HMAC-SHA-256 holds up against Grover, and the auth path is only as strong as the server's SCRAM-vs-MD5 choice (both ship in postgres-protocol). See the separate Postgres-auth finding at components/postgres/src/lib.rs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped capability: sha2 links into the indexer binaries via the transitive graph (rust-bitcoin/secp256k1 side); no first-party `use sha2` or Sha256:: call exists (grep clean across all components). SHA-256 is Grover-halved, not Shor-broken — an A-rated, near-quantum-safe posture; presence-only row.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The AEAD protects the indexer's outbound TLS traffic only; the one live client (components/bitcoind build_http_client) disables certificate verification, so GCM's integrity guarantee is undermined at the authentication layer for any https RPC URL. No first-party ring:: call; AEAD keys arrive over classical ECDHE.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev toolchain only; the generated client ships isomorphic-fetch as its sole runtime dependency, so this AE scheme is not in the published package. Related object LIB-0469707e (tweetnacl) is the library providing it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto library available in the build's dev tree; not shipped in the published client (runtime deps: isomorphic-fetch only). Provides Ed25519/X25519/XSalsa20-Poly1305 — see related object ALG-f58a8f00 for the secretbox primitive.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transport-security provider for the bitcoind RPC client, ordinals data fetches and indexer HTTP calls. rustls 0.21.x has no post-quantum key exchange; migration needs rustls ≥0.23 with the X25519MLKEM-768 hybrid — see the separate finding for the RPC channel where certificate verification is additionally disabled.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The sessions it serves are the indexer's outbound HTTPS; harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure is low-value here (chain data is public) but the channel authentication depends on it — see the bitcoind RPC finding where verification is disabled.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Classically-collision-broken hash shipping in the binaries; zero first-party call sites (no `use md5`/Md5 anywhere in components). Carried in by the resolved dependency graph rather than by any workspace declaration. Presence-only: a CBOM reader should know MD5 ships even though nothing here invokes it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Changeable here by dependency upgrade (and required as the substrate for any future PQ-hybrid rustls); no first-party direct use of ring APIs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: hashing capability present in the runtime tree of the API server, currently dead code — see the separate bitcoinjs-lib finding (api/ordinals/package.json:66) which is the parent that pulls it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped dev-tree crypto library (ECDSA/ECDH helpers over P-256/P-384/secp256k1 via bn.js/hash.js). Not imported by API source; bitcoinjs-lib v6 does not depend on it. Kept as the library-level row — ALG-710f61f0 records the ECDSA capability this package provides; this row records that the package itself ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA256-class MAC capability in the shipped binaries; no first-party Hmac/use hmac call site (grep clean). Presence-only row — a quantum-safe (Grover-limited) primitive carried by the resolved dependency graph rather than by a workspace declaration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JS hash implementations (MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256/RIPEMD-160) bundled for the docs generator's browser polyfill chain; dev-tree only, not imported by API source. Presence row for the shipped dev install.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The npm pbkdf2 package itself (browser PBKDF2, defaulting to SHA-1 in the polyfill unless its caller overrides); dev-tree only. No runtime or first-party use — the library ships with the dev install the docs toolchain builds; ALG-4de3b020 is its algorithm row.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Rust SHA-2 provider in the shipped indexer binaries; primarily exercised through the Postgres SCRAM auth handshake (components/postgres/src/lib.rs).
